messages.subject: Accounting for No Observations
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I've read in some other threads in the help forums that to account for an=
instance of no observations on a line transect, your distance data shoul=
d include information on the transect walked followed by a blank for the =
perpendicular distance to observation. I have formatted my data according=
ly, and everything seems to be fine with the data import, but when I view=
my imported data in Distance, these blank records are not visible. Am I =
missing a step in importing the data? Or perhaps these records exist but =
are not being displayed as they are blank? I'm relatively new to Distance=

, and not sure why this would be happening.

Thank you for your help,

Kelly O'Connor

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Accounting for No Observations
parts:
Kelly:

You ought to see a row in the data table without data in the
'Observation layer' that corresponds to transects you walked without
registering any sightings. I will show you a screen capture offline
(Jiscmail does not allow sending attachments) of how your data should
appear inside Distance.

Meanwhile you can look for yourself by opening the sample project
"Stratify example.dst" that can be found in the "Sample Projects"
directory when you open Distance. Look at transects 5 and 6.

In addition to this you can view a brief description of the data import
process at this web location

http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance.workshops/distance2013/preparingdata.html

showing a transect without sightings (line 1 in stratum 2).

Finally, the URL above also points you to a narrated video that you can
watch and listen to (if you are willing to use a Java plugin on your
computer) demonstrating the data import process.
